title: Machine Learning for Forecasting
interviewAnswer: Tree/boosting models can forecast by transforming temporal history into supervised features such as lags, rolling statistics, calendar variables and exogenous drivers. Backtesting must preserve temporal order and feature availability.
keyPoints: Global models can learn across many related series.
Recursive vs direct multi-step strategies differ.
Feature leakage is a major risk.
why: Machine Learning for Forecasting appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Global models can learn across many related series.
deepDive: Tree/boosting models can forecast by transforming temporal history into supervised features such as lags, rolling statistics, calendar variables and exogenous drivers. Backtesting must preserve temporal order and feature availability. Recursive vs direct multi-step strategies differ. Feature leakage is a major risk. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Train LightGBM across thousands of SKUs using lag/rolling/calendar features and rolling-origin validation.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Machine Learning for Forecasting make?
How would you validate or debug Machine Learning for Forecasting in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
